correctness.rationale: Every square has 0 or 2 ones and is either unary or a root-offset square around a one-to-one zero gap; these cases prove the exact pointwise formula (1). For distinct gaps the constrained objective reduces to n-2(x+y)+floor(c/2); the congruence on x,y and a strict loss bound for all alternate pairs proves uniqueness. All repeated and noncontaining cases have explicit strict upper bounds for n>=25. Exhaustive arithmetic enumeration covers n=3..24 and identifies the n=30 first excess; weight <=2 is bounded separately. The actual packaged standalone checker independently exhausts 7140 literal factor instances and 669920 finite candidate maximizations, with 300 seeded longer tests. Finite experiments are not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The older same-family pointwise square formula is explicitly prior and covers each individual gap triple; this is not claimed as new. The accepted claim is the exact fixed-circumference global maximization, all sharp balanced gap triples and two oriented rotation classes, a sharp 7/6 limiting density, and first above-circumference length 30. The parent result does not state or prove these constrained extrema; obtaining them requires a global congruence-and-inequality optimization including nonbalanced and repeated-gap competitors. Public four-run extrema, linear fixed-three marker square counts and universal circular upper bounds address different domains or nonsharp quantities. A parent formula allowing finite brute-force optimization remains a material priority risk; an unindexed earlier maximization cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: This is a complete sharp constrained extremal classification for a natural sparse circular-string repetition diversity invariant. It proves that exactly two oriented necklace classes achieve the bound at every n>=25, that the optimal density is 7/6 (different from unrestricted 3/2 and sparse two-marker behavior), and that n=30 with gaps 8,9,10 is the first three-marker word with more distinct squares than positions. Integer congruence rigidity and repeated-gap exclusion explain the structural phenomenon, not just a restatement of the pointwise census.
